question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP tools/call of aws___list_regions sent as its own request: no credential, no Mcp-Session-Id header, and no initialize on this connection. Repeated with aws___search_documentation.

decoded.body: a JSON-RPC error object, code -32600, message "Session ID is required for this operation. Please include a valid session ID in your request headers or initialize a new session first."
decoded.both-tools: the same body for aws___list_regions and for aws___search_documentation with search_phrase "S3 bucket versioning"; sections 7 and 8 of the transcript
decoded.contrast: the same server answers a sessionless tools/list with the full tool list, and answers both of these tool calls with real content when the session id from a keyless initialize is sent

finding: A tools/call sent without a session is refused, and the refusal is inside a 200. The HTTP status line says OK, the content-type says application/json, and the body is a JSON-RPC error, code -32600, "Session ID is required for this operation". The boundary here is the handshake, not the credential: the same two calls succeed when a keyless initialize's session id is sent back. A client, or a survey, that reads status lines rather than bodies would record this server as answering everything, and would be wrong about which requests it answers.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -m 40 -X POST https://aws-mcp.us-east-1.api.aws/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"aws___list_regions","arguments":{}}}'
